production.note: US model years. Consumer Guide (Tom Appel) covers the '2000-05 Toyota MR2 Spyder': Toyota 'launched a mid-engined, rear-drive, two-passenger sports car as a late 2000 model', and the 2005 model is described as 'its final year'.

body.note: 'a mid-engined, rear-drive, two-passenger sports car' with a folding soft top; no fixed-roof version of the ZZW30 was sold in the US, so it is a Roadster.

configuration.note: '1.8-liter double overhead cam (DOHC) 16-valve 4-cylinder with Variable Valve Timing with intelligence (VVT-i)' (1ZZ-FED)

aspiration.note: Inferred: the brochure describes a DOHC VVT-i 4-cylinder with no turbocharger or supercharger.

drivetrain.note: 'Drivetrain: Mid-engine, rear-wheel drive with 5-speed manual transmission'

transmission.note: The 5-speed manual was the only transmission at launch (brochure: 'Mid-engine, rear-wheel drive with 5-speed manual transmission'). Consumer Guide: 'A 5-speed sequential manual gearbox became available for 2002 and was upgraded to 6-speeds in '03'. Toyota's SMT is a clutch-pedal-free automated manual.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower: 138 hp @ 6,400 rpm". Consumer Guide gives the same 138 hp for the generation ('Tuned to deliver 138 horsepower', cg-mr2-spyder-2000-05).

weightLb.note: 5-speed manual, standard equipment, 2001 model. Quote: "Curb weight (lbs.): 2,195". No manufacturer figure for the 2000 launch year was opened, so the reference year is 2001, the first year with a qualifying figure.

sources.publisher: Toyota Motor Sales, U.S.A. (brochure hosted by auto-brochures.com)
